title: Implement frozen automatic portfolio execution mode
description:
Implement story plx-428482 through outside-in specifications and the existing portfolio-run architecture.

Binding decisions:
- Add execution_mode with exactly automatic and approval_required values.
- The checked-in periodic portfolio procedure defaults execution_mode to automatic.
- Lower-level orchestration remains fail-safe for callers that omit the mode; compatibility behavior must be specified explicitly.
- Normalize and freeze execution_mode in run_spec, checkpoints, evidence fingerprints, and resume validation so a retry cannot change authorization semantics.
- In automatic mode, do not create a blocking optimization-approval ChatMessage. Treat deterministic policy selection as launch authorization only for targets with complete target-level diagnosis/readiness and current freshness, configuration, champion, feedback watermark, and cooldown evidence.
- Reuse existing optimizer dispatch and exact limits; do not bypass optimization.run validation or create another dispatch path.
- Advisory stakeholder, collection, repair, and ambiguity actions remain visible and non-launching.
- Incomplete, contradictory, stale, cooldown, structurally blocked, or otherwise unsafe targets remain rejected independently with explicit reasons.
- Never automatically promote a champion or mutate guidelines/feedback settings.
- Project execution_mode and automatic selected/launched/rejected counts and reasons into the same living Report, workbook, scorecard exports, immutable evidence, and summaries.
- Add no GraphQL models/resources and do not monkeypatch Tactus.

Delivery sequence:
1. Add failing outside-in runner and procedure contract specifications.
2. Implement frozen mode normalization and automatic target authorization.
3. Extend Report/workbook projections and reconciliation tests.
4. Run focused cross-repo and dashboard validation.
5. Obtain independent review before technical acceptance.

Do not implement until the active bounded dogfood run has produced its next durable evidence.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implementation wave started after explicit Product Owner authorization while the bounded dogfood run continues independently. Disjoint ownership: one coding agent owns procedure/runner execution-mode semantics; one owns Report/workbook/dashboard projection against the fixed execution_decisions contract. Both must begin with failing outside-in specifications, preserve the running process, add no resources, and return uncommitted completion reports. Independent review follows integration.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implementation and independent review complete; issue remains open until the change lands. The periodic procedure now defaults to frozen automatic execution while direct runner omission remains fail-safe approval-required. Automatic policy selects only independently complete targets, reuses existing freshness/limit validation and durable dispatch, skips blocking optimizer approval, preserves advisory actions, and never promotes automatically. Durable execution decisions include per-target launch status and aggregate counts derived together from exact owned child evidence; unknown or incomplete launch states remain unlaunched. The same Report, workbook, exports, and dashboard show automatic mode, selected/launched/rejected counts and reasons, plus explicit named-detail coverage without exposing opaque IDs. Two independent review rounds resolved false launch accounting, missing per-target launch status, aggregate/detail mismatch disclosure, and whitespace-only authority identifiers. Final focused evidence: 206 combined portfolio/Report/YAML/lifecycle tests, 16 authority edge tests, 20 dashboard tests, and dashboard typechecks pass; diff check is clean and no Amplify resource file changed. No commit, push, deploy, or production optimizer occurred.
